# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds, about $199 (list $299)**
- Runner's World's top pick. WIRED praises the clear sound and the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run.
- Battery is about 7 hours per charge with an IPX4 rating, so skip them for heavy rain or very long runs.
- Runner's World says Bose plans a new pair soon, so you may want to wait or watch for discounts.
- Buy: [Runner's World guide with Bose, Amazon and Walmart links](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, $125-$180**
- Your ears stay fully open, and it has 12 hours of battery and an IP55 rating. WIRED rated it 8/10 for running.
- The neckband can interfere with long hair and winter hats.
- Buy: [WIRED review with Amazon, REI and Best Buy links](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

**Best for long runs and rain: Shokz OpenDots 2, $200**
- Battery lasts 10 hours per charge (40 with the case), and the IP57 rating is the strongest in these guides. WIRED's top overall pick.
- Buy: [WIRED guide with Amazon, Best Buy and Shokz links](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best value: Soundcore AeroFit 2, about $80-$104**
- SoundGuys' budget pick. It has an IP55 rating, 10 hours of battery per charge and a 42-hour case.
- SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 on Amazon. Dealectric lists $129.99 at Soundcore's own store, or $104 with code AFSC20, which they say they tested. Check the final price at checkout.
- Buy: [Soundcore's store via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2) (an affiliate link) or [SoundGuys' open-ear roundup](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) for the Amazon link.

**Best cheap tries**
- **JLab Flex Open, about $40:** Runner's World's budget pick. Sound is less detailed, but it's comfortable and stays put. [Link](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- **SoundPeats PearlClip Pro, $50:** WIRED's cheap pick, good for finding out whether you like clip-ons. [Link](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Also worth a look: Nothing Ear (Open), about $99 on Amazon.** SoundGuys named it best open-ear overall, and its workout guide picks it as best for running. It has an IP54 rating and strong bass for the category. [Link](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Quick guide**
- Maximum awareness: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.
- Best sound: Bose Ultra Open.
- Rain or marathon training: Shokz OpenDots 2.
- Tight budget: JLab Flex Open or AeroFit 2.

Open-ear earbuds are less safe in loud traffic if you turn them up. Runner's World notes the Bose can feel quiet in busy city traffic, and no open-ear design guarantees you'll hear everything. Prices change often, so confirm at checkout.
